metais ls — List the entries under a path of a package.

Usage:
  metais ls <package> [<path>] [--recursive | -r] [--limit <name>=<value>]...
            [--json]

With no path, lists the root. A path that names a directory lists its children,
or with --recursive every file and directory beneath it; a path that names a
file lists that file. Directories are implied by the entries' paths. The listing
is in the byte order of the paths, a directory's written with its trailing /.

A packed package's entries are the zip's, .compiled/ included; a source
directory's are the files metais pack would write from it, without .compiled/.
Paths use / on every platform and are matched byte for byte, case-sensitively;
the root is . or omitted.

Operands:
  <package>
      A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a
      package is read with random access. Required.
  <path>
      An entry or a directory of the package, with or without a trailing /; the
      root when omitted.

Flags:
  -r, --recursive
      List every file and directory beneath the path, not only its children.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  One line per entry: its type (file or dir), a file's size in bytes or the
  number of files beneath a directory, and its path, separated by tabs. With
  --json, one metais.ls/1 document.

Refusals:
  limit.invalid
      A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.
      Next: metais limits
  limit.package
      The package breaches one of its limits.
      Next: metais limits
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais ls --help
  usage.entry_not_found
      The path names no entry and no directory of the package.
      Next: metais ls <package> <path>
  usage.missing_operand
      The package operand is not given.
      Next: metais ls --help
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais ls --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais ls --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais ls --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais ls --help

  Each line below is a family of codes: how many there are, the cause they share
  and their next step. 'metais help refusals ls' lists every code, and help
  --json gives each code's own cause.

  manifest.* (60)  The manifest breaks one of its rules.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>
  package.* (46)   The package is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  schema.* (10)    An input schema is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  template.* (9)   An output's path, when or for_each does not parse.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>

Examples:
  metais ls report-1.0.0.metais
      Lists the package's top level.
  metais ls report-1.0.0.metais references/ -r
      Lists everything beneath references/.
  metais ls report-1.0.0.metais --json
      Prints the listing as one metais.ls/1 document.
